criterionVerdicts.reasoning: All three valid naive-user personas reached the end state and reported goalAchieved=true, and I confirmed the artifacts myself rather than taking the reports on trust. spec-auditor/shots/19-requested.png shows the project page after confirm with the toast 'Adopted — 5 journeys written into .ligma/' and a Knowledge tab whose boot recipe is sourced from /Users/alexraymond/ligma-classic/.ligma/boot.json, marked 'ready'; naive-user-3/shots/63-click.png shows the same shape for a second, different repo (mission-control) plus a recorded behaviour baseline held under a 'Baselines' section that reads 'recorded centrally and never in the repo'. naive-user-1/shots/31-requested.png shows the honest empty counterpart ('No characterization baselines yet') for a project where no journey was proved, so the populated states are not boilerplate. The caveat is the 'without help' clause: no persona got through on the first inferred recipe. naive-user-1 needed five recipe attempts ending in an npx+PATH workaround it described as one 'a normal user would never find'; naive-user-3 needed pnpm's --ignore-workspace flag twice. The outcome the criterion describes was reached every time, but only via developer-level toolchain knowledge — raised as a human decision rather than scored as a failure, since each persona did in fact accomplish it unaided by a human.

spec-auditor/shots/03-click.png is the home page ('What are we making?') in 'Adopt a repo' mode with /Users/alexraymond/ligma-classic typed in, and the helper text 'A run will infer the boot recipe and propose journeys — you confirm them on one sheet.' spec-auditor/shots/19-requested.png shows the resulting project 'ligma-classic' created and Active. naive-user-2 adopted the same checkout independently (personas/naive-user-2/shots/39-requested.png, project ligma-classic) and naive-user-3 adopted a second pre-existing repo, mission-control (personas/naive-user-3/shots/67-goto.png), so this is not a one-repo special case. All entry points were the home page.

The interaction shape the criterion asks for exists and carried every persona through: spec-auditor/shots/06-requested.png shows the system's own inferred boot recipe (appDir, install, dev, portStrategy, healthPath, healthMarker) with a written rationale and a single 'Correct it' escape hatch — the user is not authoring a config from scratch — and spec-auditor/shots/18-click.png shows the single terminal control, 'Adopt this repo', with the footer 'One confirm writes .ligma/ into the repo and creates the project.' naive-user-3/shots/70-goto.png confirms the confirmed recipe landed at /Users/alexraymond/mission-control/.ligma/boot.json marked 'ready'. Against that: in 0 of 4 observed adoptions was the first inference correct. spec-auditor and naive-user-2 both had to change a port (5173→5174), naive-user-3 needed --ignore-workspace twice, naive-user-1 needed five attempts. The correction UI is a raw JSON textarea, which is closer to 'filling in a form' than the criterion's promise. I score the mechanism met and flag the inference hit-rate as a human decision.

spec-auditor/shots/16-click.png shows 'Proposed journeys 0 of 5 accepted' generated by the crawl, each with a user-facing title ('Turn a prompt into a design'), a plain-language goal, a 'Why' paragraph citing what the crawler actually saw in the repo's UI, and numbered steps — i.e. proposals derived from exploring the repo, not a fixed template. naive-user-3 got 6 proposals for a completely different repo, phrased in that repo's domain terms ('Answer the decisions my crew escalates to me', 'Plan and prioritize work with the Eisenhower matrix' — personas/naive-user-3/shots/67-goto.png), which rules out canned output. spec-auditor/shots/18-click.png additionally shows a 'Confusion log' — the crawl's own UX audit of what it could not work out.

spec-auditor/shots/16-click.png shows the review sheet before any write: each proposal is individually editable (title and goal in text fields) and individually Accepted/Rejected, with 'Accept all' / 'Reject all', alongside the editable project name, shape, and the boot recipe. spec-auditor/shots/18-click.png shows the sheet's foot stating 'One confirm writes .ligma/ into the repo and creates the project' next to the 'Adopt this repo' button — so nothing is written until review is complete — and spec-auditor/shots/19-requested.png is the post-confirm state with the toast 'Adopted — 5 journeys written into .ligma/'. naive-user-3 exercised the editing affordance (their sheet reads '6 of 6 accepted' after review) and naive-user-1 independently confirmed .ligma/ appeared in the repo only on confirm.

spec-auditor/shots/31-requested.png is the project's Verify tab listing the journeys, each tagged 'PROPOSED BY CRAWL' with its goal text, a smoke selector and a 'Prove it' button. Corroborated on two other projects: naive-user-2/shots/39-requested.png (ligma-classic, 5 journeys) and naive-user-3/shots/67-goto.png (mission-control, 6 journeys, titles matching that repo's proposals). One defect on this surface, reported by spec-auditor and visible in their shot: re-adopting a repo whose .ligma/ already holds journeys merges without dedup, so 5 accepted proposals produced 8 rows including near-duplicate pairs ('Figure out what went wrong' vs 'Diagnose problems and report a bug'). The criterion — Verify populated with the proposed journeys — is still met; the duplication is raised as a human decision.

spec-auditor/shots/19-requested.png shows the Knowledge tab immediately post-adopt carrying the boot recipe (path, app dir, install, dev, port, health marker, 'ready' badge) and a project.md beginning '# Project notes / ## Quirks'. spec-auditor/shots/40-requested.png shows the rest of that page: the crawl's confusion log rendered as minor/note entries, the Journeys list, and the Baselines section. naive-user-3/shots/63-click.png shows the equivalent for mission-control with repo-specific notes (crew skills contradiction, hydration-mismatch errors, /daemon 404), so the content is genuinely derived from each repo rather than scaffolding.

I am overriding the spec-auditor's not-met here, because two other personas produced traceable affirmative evidence and the auditor's failure is a capacity failure rather than the product doing something else. naive-user-3 clicked 'Prove it' on the Verify surface at 09:00:12.9 (steps.jsonl step 81, personas/naive-user-3/shots/39-click.png), polled for ~30 minutes, and then saw the journey chip flip to 'done' with 'Last run 2026-08-12 09:00' (personas/naive-user-3/shots/67-goto.png) and a baseline in Knowledge: 'jrn_capture-a-thought-and-turn-it-into-a-task — 20 steps · 337s on task · 0 wrong turns — recorded by vrun_1786525213503' with substantive behaviour findings (personas/naive-user-3/shots/63-click.png). vrun_1786525213503 decodes to 09:00:13Z, exactly their click — the baseline is provably the product of that Prove-it, not inherited history. The same check holds for naive-user-2: their click at 07:56:45.7 produced baseline 'recorded by vrun_1786521406438' (= 07:56:46Z), visible in personas/spec-auditor/shots/40-requested.png. The spec-auditor's own attempt did fail after ~45 minutes with 'Harness malfunction — governor denied persona returning-user for 20min (last reason: reserve)' at 32/40 sessions and 0 free, and recorded no baseline; that is a real reliability defect (roughly 1 in 3 attempts here) and is raised as a human decision, but it is quota exhaustion caused by the two earlier successful proofs, not the surface failing to do the promised thing.

Both halves are visible on the Knowledge surface. Central store: the Baselines section states 'What working currently looks like, recorded centrally and never in the repo — a builder that could read these could teach to the test. Read-only,' and each entry links out to the central verification run that produced it ('recorded by vrun_1786525213503' → /verification/<runId>) rather than to any repo path — personas/naive-user-3/shots/63-click.png and personas/spec-auditor/shots/40-requested.png. Repo side: the same page shows .ligma/ carrying exactly the boot recipe (path /Users/alexraymond/ligma-classic/.ligma/boot.json), the journeys, and project.md notes, with no behaviour record among them (personas/spec-auditor/shots/19-requested.png), and the adopt toast said '5 journeys written into .ligma/'. naive-user-1 independently checked the filesystem and reported the repo gained only .ligma/ with no baseline files. The honest empty state in personas/naive-user-1/shots/31-requested.png ('No characterization baselines yet') shows the section reflects real central data rather than static copy.

humanDecisions.question: Boot-recipe inference was wrong on the first try in 4 of 4 adoptions, and recovery means hand-editing raw JSON. Is 'confirm once' acceptable when nobody actually confirmed once?
humanDecisions.context: spec-auditor and naive-user-2 both had to change the port (inference pinned 5173, rationale calling it 'the only honest strategy', while the dev server bound 5174 — and the correct port was sitting in the dev-server log the product itself displayed). naive-user-3 hit a pnpm workspace failure twice and needed --ignore-workspace. naive-user-1 needed five attempts, ending in an npx+PATH workaround it described as one a normal user would never find, because the environment overrode the repo's pinned pnpm/Node even when given absolute paths. Each failure costs an install, a boot and a 120s health poll, and the only explanation offered is raw pnpm stderr — in naive-user-1's case advising 'install the required pnpm version globally' when it already was. The single-confirm sheet exists and works; the question is whether the inference hit-rate makes it real.

humanDecisions.question: A user-initiated 'Prove it' can be starved by the governor. Should proofs get access to the user reserve before this ships?
humanDecisions.context: spec-auditor's proof ran ~45 minutes, consumed quota 29→32 of 40 sessions, then ended in 'error — Harness malfunction — not a verdict — governor denied persona returning-user for 20min (last reason: reserve)' with no baseline recorded. Two earlier proofs (naive-user-2, naive-user-3) succeeded and recorded baselines — they are what exhausted the budget. So on a busy day the Verify surface silently cannot do the one thing crit_7 asks of it.

humanDecisions.question: Proof runs are invisible while they run. Accept, or block on making them watchable?
humanDecisions.context: All three personas who proved a journey reported the same thing independently: the Verify chip says 'running' and the Governor gauge climbs, but the global Runs page and the project's Runs tab both say '0 running' for the full ~30 minutes, despite copy promising 'Every agent session, live' and the adoption sheet promising proofs are 'watchable like any other run on Runs'. naive-user-3's run page showed a bare 'Running' with empty [REDACTED] tabs for 30 minutes, and the absence of any acknowledgement on click led them to click 'Prove it' a second time.

humanDecisions.question: Re-adopting a repo that already has .ligma/ journeys merges without dedup, and the new project silently inherits the previous adoption's run history. Intended continuity or a bug?
humanDecisions.context: spec-auditor's 5 accepted proposals produced a Verify surface with 8 journeys including three near-duplicate pairs ('Ground designs in my codebase's design system' vs 'Ground generated designs in my repo's design system'). The same freshly-created project also arrived with a 'done' verdict chip, a 'Last run 07:56' link, a populated regression corpus and a central baseline — all from the earlier persona's adoption of the same repo, with nothing on screen explaining where that history came from.

humanDecisions.question: Two label collisions on the adopt form silently discard the user's typed repo path. Cheap fix worth doing before this is the front door?
humanDecisions.context: All three naive personas hit it: the 'Adopt a repo' mode toggle sits next to the 'Adopt' submit button and the labels overlap as substrings, so a click aimed at submit lands on the toggle, resets the form and drops the path with no feedback. Separately, naive-user-2 found that submitting a path the adopter rejects (a directory nested in another git repo) returns HTTP 400 with no visible error anywhere in the UI. During a successful adoption the page shows only the word 'crawling' for 10+ minutes with no stage or progress indicator.

humanDecisions.question: Two timestamp/duration display bugs — worth fixing before launch, or after?
humanDecisions.context: naive-user-3 found the journey card reporting 'Last run 2026-08-12 09:00' while that same run's page said it started at 10:00:13 AM — an hour apart, so the user cannot tell when the run happened. spec-auditor found completed runs' durations growing with wall-clock time (the same finished adoption showed '25m 21s total', then '45m 56s', and an older done run climbed from '2h 19m' to '2h 51m'), i.e. duration computed against now rather than the run's end time.

humanDecisions.question: The returning-user persona produced no usable evidence. Re-run before accepting, or accept single-session coverage?
humanDecisions.context: 1 of 5 persona runs (returning-user) is invalid — 29 steps, no findings, goalAchieved null. That charter is the one that would have tested whether the surfaces hold up on a later visit, so crit_5, crit_6 and crit_8 rest entirely on observations made within the same session that created them, and crit_7's persistence across a return visit is untested. Every verdict above therefore reflects first-session behaviour only; nothing here demonstrates that Verify, Knowledge or the central baselines still read correctly when a user comes back to the project later.
